subject: Clarify: multi-entity remittances, nostro tagging & intermediary fee handling
messages:
From: Accounts Payable <accounts-payable@brightlinehealth.com>
To: diego@redwoodinference.com
Cc: finance@brightlinehealth.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Payment instructions and intermediary fee question (INV-202706-12345)

Hi Diego,

We're preparing settlement for the June invoices (attached) and have a couple of questions before sending the wires:

1) We have two invoices that need to be paid to Redwood: INV-202706-12345 (USD, Redwood Inference, Inc.) and INV-202706-67890 (EUR, Redwood EU Ops LTD). Our bank can either send two separate wires or one consolidated payment. Do you have a preference? If consolidated, what remittance tags should we include so you can allocate across legal entities?

2) Intermediary (correspondent) bank fees: some of our partner banks route payments through a London correspondent and they will deduct an intermediary fee before Redwood receives funds. Should we instruct our bank to use OUR / SHA / BEN for each wire? If the intermediary fee is deducted, do you want us to gross-up the invoice so you receive the full invoice amount net of those deductions, or would you prefer to receive a net payment and have Redwood absorb the intermediary fee? Any guidance on how you classify/reclaim VAT on those fees would also help.

3) Our bank requires an "Ultimate Debtor/Beneficiary reference" field when we send cross-border payments for reconciliation. Please tell us the exact text to put in that field (company name + TAX ID or invoice reference).

I've attached the invoice and our recent outgoing bank statement showing the expected fee path. We're aiming to execute the payment tomorrow morning (20 Jul).

Thanks,
Marta Castillo
Accounts Payable
Brightline Health
attachments: Brightline_INV-202706-12345.pdf, Brightline_bank_statement_JUN2027.csv
From: diego@redwoodinference.com
To: Accounts Payable <accounts-payable@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payment instructions and intermediary fee question (INV-202706-12345)

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear note and attachments. Quick answers and recommended path below so your treasury team can proceed tomorrow.

Short answers:
- Preferred: send two separate wires (one USD to Redwood Inference, Inc.; one EUR to Redwood EU Ops LTD). This avoids manual allocation and reduces reconciliation effort.
- If you must send a single consolidated wire, please include explicit remittance tags for each invoice: INV-202706-12345 (USD) / INV-202706-67890 (EUR) and add the legal entity string as shown below in the "Ultimate Debtor/Remit Tag" field. We'll sweep to the appropriate ledgers once funds post.
- Charge handling: where possible, please instruct YOUR (sender pays all charges). We understand some banks can't guarantee OUR due to correspondent constraints. If YOUR/OUR is not available, use SHA and include a separate remittance line called "EXPECTED_CORRESP_FEES: <amount-estimate>" so we can follow up. If your bank will deduct intermediary fees and you cannot gross-up, please notify us immediately and we'll reconcile on receipt.

Suggested wire fields (please copy these exactly into the payment order):

-- USD wire (Redwood Inference, Inc.) --
Beneficiary name: Redwood Inference, Inc.
Beneficiary account: [US ACCOUNT / ACH - see portal]
Beneficiary address: 235 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94105, USA
Beneficiary tax id: 94-XXXXXXX
Intermediary / Correspondent bank (if required): Citibank N.A., London Branch (SWIFT: CITIGB2LXXX) -- Use only if your bank requires a correspondent.
Beneficiary bank: First Cupertino Bank, NY (SWIFT: FCBNUS33XXX)
Payment details / remittance: INV-202706-12345; UltimateDebtor=Brightline Health|TaxID=BR-4523456
Charges indicator: OUR (preferred) / SHA (acceptable if OUR not available)

-- EUR wire (Redwood EU Ops LTD) --
Beneficiary name: Redwood EU Ops LTD
IBAN: GB29NWBK60161331926819 (example IBAN — please follow the IBAN provided in the invoice PDF)
BIC/SWIFT: NWBKGB2LXXX
Beneficiary address: 41-45 Bloomsbury St, London, UK
Payment details / remittance: INV-202706-67890; UltimateDebtor=Brightline Health|VATReg=GB123456789
Charges indicator: SHA (many EUR rails don't support OUR reliably)

Notes on VAT and fee recovery:
- Intermediary bank fees themselves are banking service charges and are generally not subject to VAT when charged by the bank. They are not part of the taxable base for our product invoices.
- If an intermediary fee is deducted before funds reach us, we will record that as a banking expense and will not reclaim VAT on the fee (since it is a bank service). If you gross-up to cover the fee, we will reconcile and treat the additional receipt as a reimbursement and document it accordingly.

If you confirm you can do separate wires with the fields above, we'll confirm ledger posting instructions and provide a short remittance template for your treasury, otherwise send the consolidated payment with the detailed tags and we'll handle mapping on our side.

I'll loop finance ops (Laura) to confirm accounting treatment and provide the remittance-template.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
To: diego@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payment instructions and intermediary fee question (INV-202706-12345)

Diego / Marissa — FYI and a couple of accounting clarifications I want on record before we ask the customer to proceed:

1) Allocation & Sweep: If Brightline sends a single consolidated wire with the remittance tags suggested, our treasury sweep will use the "UltimateDebtor" tag to allocate to the correct legal entity. Please ensure the remittance template has the exact pipe-delimited format (InvoiceID; UltimateDebtor=NAME|TaxID=xxx) so our automated parser picks it up.

2) Fee treatment: For USD receipts where OUR is not available and intermediary fees are deducted by corres banks, we should do the following: 
  - Post the receipt for the gross invoice amount to revenue, post the bank fee as a separate bank charge (GL: Bank Fees).
  - Do not gross-up revenue for bank fees unless the customer explicitly reimburses them and the payment instructions included a separate "EXPECTED_CORRESP_FEES" field and the actual fee matches that estimate.

3) VAT: If Brightline is an EU payer and this is a supply that qualifies for reverse charge, they should include their VAT reg number in the remittance tag. Our tax team will handle the reverse-charge reporting. If they gross-up to cover fees, that reimbursement is outside of the VAT-able consideration for the invoiced service (bank fees are not VAT vendor-supplied services for our taxable base).

I'll attach the remittance-template and a short note for treasury with the exact parser examples.

Laura Bennett
Head of Finance Ops
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-remittance-template.xlsx

Subject: Re: Payment instructions and intermediary fee question (INV-202706-12345)

Diego / Laura — thanks for the detail and template. Confirming the plan from our side:

- We'll split into two wires as recommended: USD for INV-202706-12345 and EUR for INV-202706-67890.
- For the USD wire, Treasury will attempt OUR. If OUR is not supported by our bank's correspondent path, we will send SHA and include an "EXPECTED_CORRESP_FEES" line with our estimate.
- For the EUR wire, we'll send SHA and include Brightline's VAT reg in the UltimateDebtor tag as requested.
- Remittance tags will exactly match the format: INV-202706-12345; UltimateDebtor=Brightline Health|TaxID=BR-4523456

We'll run both payments early tomorrow local time and will share the outgoing confirmations (SWIFT MT103 / payment adv) so you can reconcile on receipt. If Redwood sees a material deduction on arrival, please let us know and we'll investigate with our bank.

Best,
Marta Castillo
Accounts Payable
Brightline Health
